title: Does sauna sweating remove arsenic, cadmium, lead, or mercury?

grade.title: Small, uncontrolled, or single-source human evidence
grade.outcome: Sweat as a route that contains metals
grade.basis: One case series and one systematic review. No clinical outcome.

answerHtml: A 20-person case series found arsenic, cadmium, lead, mercury, and other elements in sweat, sometimes at higher levels than in urine or blood. A review of 24 studies called for adequately sized trials. Detectable metal in sweat is not evidence that sauna use lowers body burden or improves health.

sections.heading: Studies
sections.html:
• Genuis 2011: 20 adults. Elements were detectable in sweat. PMID 21057782.
  • Sears 2012: review of 24 studies. Authors call for adequately sized trials. PMID 22505948. A DOI recorded in the draft table was marked unverified and is not used.
